Spatial cross-validation of conductance formulas on a fixed graph

Source: R/spatial_cv.R
terradish_cv_folds.Rd

Fits one or more conductance formulas to each training fold while retaining the complete landscape graph, then evaluates the trained coefficients on the held-out focal sites. Measurement parameters can be reprofiled on each test fold or held at their training estimates for predictive scoring.

Usage

terradish_cv_folds(
  data,
  formulas,
  folds,
  model = "mlpe",
  nu = NULL,
  conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
  baseline = TRUE,
  keep_fits = c("none", "slim", "full"),
  checkpoint = NULL,
  resume = TRUE,
  cores = 1L,
  measurement_control = NULL,
  nuisance = c("reprofile", "fixed"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'terradish_cv_folds'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

A prebuilt terradish_graph, usually returned by conductance_surface.

formulas

A formula or named list of formulas. All formulas must use the same response matrix and likelihood family.

folds

Fold membership for each focal site. Use terradish_folds, or supply study-specific labels. A list of fold vectors requests repeated cross-validation.

model

Measurement model function or one of "mlpe" (mlpe), "ls" (leastsquares), or "wishart". The string "wishart" selects generalized_wishart, which expects a squared-distance response. For a covariance-matrix response pass the function itself, model = wishart_covariance. With fixed nuisance parameters, a named list matching the formula names can compare models within one family.

nu

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom when required by the selected measurement model.

conductance_model

One conductance-model factory or a named list matching the formula names, allowing log-linear, Gaussian, and spline models in the same comparison.

baseline

Should each test fold also be scored at zero conductance coefficients, the uniform-conductance baseline on the same graph?

keep_fits

Whether to retain no training fits, slim fits, or full fits.

checkpoint

Optional file path. Completed fold results are written atomically after every successful or failed fit so a long run can be inspected or resumed.

resume

Logical. If TRUE and checkpoint exists, continue a compatible run without reevaluating completed formula-fold combinations.

cores

Number of workers used inside each model fit. Fold evaluation is serial to avoid nested parallel clusters.

measurement_control

Optional NewtonRaphsonControl object for profiling nuisance parameters.

nuisance

"reprofile" (default) estimates measurement parameters separately on each held-out block. "fixed" holds every measurement parameter, including environmental coefficients, at its training estimate.

...

Additional arguments passed to terradish. An explicit optimizer is used for each training fit. Otherwise the training call tries Newton and retries with BFGS if Newton raises an error. For print(), further arguments passed to the data-frame print method.

x

An object of class "terradish_cv_folds", for print().

Value

An object of class "terradish_cv_folds". Its folds element records the site assignments, results contains one row per formula and fold, and summary reports summed and mean held-out scores by formula, common-fold totals, paired differences from the best model, the standard error of their mean, and a one-standard-error flag. Repeated runs also report the SD of repeat totals over common folds. Optional retained fits are stored in fits. print() returns its input invisibly.

Columns of results: model, fold, repetition, n_train and n_test (sites), loglik (held-out log-likelihood of the trained model; larger is better), baseline_loglik (the same for uniform conductance), loglik_gain (their difference), nuisance_iterations and nuisance_convergence, elapsed_seconds, error and baseline_error (messages for failed fits or scores), common_fold (TRUE when every model succeeded on that fold), and paired_difference (the model's loglik minus the best model's on the same fold).

Columns of summary, which print() displays with the best model first: folds, failed, and n_folds_ok (fold counts; read these first), total_loglik and mean_loglik over all of a model's folds (NA total when any fold failed), common_folds_total and n_common_folds (the total over folds on which every model succeeded; models are ranked by this column), between_repeat_sd, total_loglik_gain and mean_loglik_gain (improvement over uniform conductance), mean_difference and se_difference (mean paired difference from the best model and its standard error across folds), and within_one_se (TRUE when that mean difference is no larger than its standard error, so the model is not clearly worse than the best one).

Details

The graph domain and raster covariates remain fixed. Only the focal-site entries of the graph (its demes index and the matching solver right-hand sides), the response matrix, and any measurement-model site attributes are subset. This evaluates transfer to held-out sites within the observed landscape rather than rebuilding a new landscape for every fold.

Reprofiled scores compare conductance formulas under one measurement model; they must not be compared across calls with different measurement models or effective degrees of freedom. Fixed-parameter scores are predictive marginal densities and can compare measurement models within one likelihood family. Neither mode scores pairs spanning training and test sites. Spatial folds score only within-cluster pairs. Wishart score gains scale with nu, although ideal fitted rankings are invariant to its scale.

Checkpoints include a signature of the response, graph, focal cells, covariates, model definitions, formulas, nu, and fold assignments. For factor covariates the signature retains class placement, levels, and contrasts. Uniform ~1 formulas are scored with unit conductance. A mismatched signature stops resumption. Nonconverged fits and failed scores count as failed folds. Training fits must record code 0 for both outer and final nuisance optimization; missing diagnostics also fail the fold. Checkpoints predating this convergence requirement are incompatible and must be recomputed (use a new checkpoint or resume = FALSE). With fixed nuisance parameters, no-structure boundary fits remain scoreable because predictions do not depend on conductance. A failed uniform-baseline score is recorded separately: model scores remain usable, but baseline gains are unavailable for that fold. Models with failed folds receive NA totals and an explicit success count. Rankings use only folds successful for every model. Paired differences and their standard errors are descriptive; repeated folds share observations and are not independent replicates.

loglik_gain is the trained model's held-out log-likelihood minus the uniform-conductance baseline log-likelihood. Larger values indicate improved prediction over that baseline. Raw log-likelihood and gain are comparable only among models using the same response representation, measurement likelihood, folds, graph, and effective degrees of freedom. They are not a common scoring rule for comparing MLPE, generalized-Wishart distance, and covariance-Wishart models.

Examples

# \donttest{
r <- terra::rast(nrows = 8, ncols = 8, xmin = 0, xmax = 8,
                 ymin = 0, ymax = 8, crs = "EPSG:32617")
terra::values(r) <- sin(seq_len(64) / 5) + seq_len(64) / 64
names(r) <- "x"
sites <- terra::xyFromCell(r, c(1, 5, 8, 12, 20, 27, 33, 37, 45, 53, 57, 64))
surface <- conductance_surface(r, sites)
response <- simulate_covariance_response(c(x = 0.8), ~x, surface,
  nu = 1000, seed = 93)$covariance
folds <- terradish_folds(sites, k = 3, method = "random", seed = 1)
cv <- terradish_cv_folds(
  surface,
  list(uniform = response ~ 1, gradient = response ~ x),
  folds = folds,
  model = wishart_covariance, nu = 1000, nuisance = "fixed",
  control = NewtonRaphsonControl(maxit = 100))
# Check fold success counts (failed, n_folds_ok) before comparing the
# common-fold predictive scores. The best model is listed first.
cv
#> Fixed-domain terradish cross-validation
#> Measurement model: wishart_covariance 
#> Repeats: 1 | nuisance: fixed 
#> Ranks use common successful folds; differences are paired against the best model.
#> 
#>     model folds failed n_folds_ok total_loglik common_folds_total
#>  gradient     3      0          3     6462.632           6462.632
#>   uniform     3      0          3     6324.266           6324.266
#>  n_common_folds between_repeat_sd mean_loglik total_loglik_gain
#>               3                NA    2154.211          138.3657
#>               3                NA    2108.089            0.0000
#>  mean_loglik_gain se_difference mean_difference within_one_se
#>          46.12189       0.00000         0.00000          TRUE
#>           0.00000      17.04508       -46.12189         FALSE
cv$summary[, c("model", "n_folds_ok", "common_folds_total",
               "mean_difference", "se_difference", "within_one_se")]
#>      model n_folds_ok common_folds_total mean_difference se_difference
#> 1 gradient          3           6462.632         0.00000       0.00000
#> 2  uniform          3           6324.266       -46.12189      17.04508
#>   within_one_se
#> 1          TRUE
#> 2         FALSE
# Random folds illustrate the call; choose ecological spatial blocks in practice.
# }
